title: Common Irregular Verbs
description: Use frequent irregular past forms in a short account.
objectives: Use frequent irregular past forms in a short account.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to use frequent irregular past forms in a short account. The central language is went, had, saw, made, took, came, and bought. It belongs to the practical context of talking about the past. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: went, had, saw, made, took, came, and bought

blocks.english: I went downtown and bought a book.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the common irregular verbs exchange.

blocks.english: We had lunch with our friends.
blocks.explanation: This common irregular verbs model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the common irregular verbs exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I went downtown and bought a book.” and “We had lunch with our friends.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: went, had, saw, made, took, came, and bought.
